title: CLARE: A Semi-supervised Community Detection Algorithm

problem.claim: Community detection seeks closely related subgraphs, but traditional algorithms fail to identify particular kinds of communities, limiting applications such as distinguishing fraud groups from normal groups in transaction networks.

gap.claim: Existing seed-based semi-supervised methods are sensitive to seed quality and have issues including inflexibility and high computational overhead.

contributions.claim: CLARE is a semi-supervised community detection algorithm with a Community Locator and a Community Rewriter.
The Community Locator quickly finds potential communities by seeking subgraphs similar to training communities.
The Community Rewriter uses deep reinforcement learning to flexibly refine community structures through decisions such as adding or dropping nodes.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments comparing CLARE with prior state-of-the-art approaches on multiple real-world datasets.
The authors report that the experiments verify the effectiveness and efficiency of CLARE.

narrative_sequence.summary: Traditional community detection cannot reliably identify certain community types needed in real-world applications.
Semi-supervised methods use labeled communities, but seed-based approaches depend on seed quality and may be inflexible or computationally expensive.
CLARE locates potential communities and then refines them using a Community Locator and a reinforcement-learning-enhanced Community Rewriter.
Experiments on multiple real-world datasets compare CLARE with prior state-of-the-art approaches and report effectiveness and efficiency.

source_observation.claim: Seed-based community detection can be affected by errors in selected seed nodes, while CLARE separates locating potential communities from refining them.

interpretation.claim: Separating candidate discovery from structural refinement may reduce dependence on any single initial seed.

application.claim: For semi-supervised graph tasks, consider a pipeline that first retrieves candidates similar to labeled examples and then applies a flexible refinement stage.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this decomposition improves robustness across different seed qualities or graph settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, evaluation metrics, baselines, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the training procedure, computational costs, or limitations of the method.
